The cost of consumer credit is rising.

The average interest rate on a US credit card rose +0.2 percentage points in August, to 22.36%, its highest level in 12 months.

This is now only 1.0 percentage point below the record 23.37% set in August 2024.

Since 2021, the average credit card interest rate has surged +6.5 percentage points.

By comparison, the 5-year average before the 2020 pandemic was 14.94%.

Meanwhile, the average interest rate on a 5-year new car loan rose +0.4 percentage points in August, to 7.54%, its highest since August 2025.

This is 3.5 percentage points above pre-pandemic levels, but 0.9 percentage points below its all-time high of 8.4%, recorded in August 2024.

Consumer borrowing has rarely been this expensive.

AI will become one of the largest spending categories in the US economy:

AI services are projected to account for a record 8.8% of US GDP in 2032.

This estimate shows how much businesses and consumers are expected to spend per year on the services of AI companies.

This also implies AI companies would generate ~$3.5 trillion in annual revenue by 2032.

By comparison, US consumer spending on food accounts for a similar 9.1% of GDP.

This figure would also be ~72% higher than energy, at 5.1% of GDP, and twice the size of construction as well as computers and software, both at 4.4%.

It would also be nearly 3x defense, at 2.8%, and more than 7x communications and internet, at 1.2% of GDP.

The only category where spending is significantly larger is health, at 18% of GDP.

The scale of the AI revolution is unlike anything seen before.

BREAKING: China’s central bank officially bought +23 tonnes of gold in September, its largest monthly purchase since September 2023.

This follows +20 tonnes purchased in both August and July, and marks its 23rd consecutive monthly gold purchase.

So far in 2026, China has officially acquired +103 tonnes of gold, raising total holdings to a record 2,410 tonnes.

China is now the world’s 5th-largest gold holder, following the US, Germany, Italy, and France.

At this pace, it could surpass Italy and France as early as this year, which hold 2,452 tonnes and 2,437 tonnes, respectively.

China is aggressively buying the dip in gold.

AI stocks are driving the entire stock market.

The "AI Winners Index" is up +58% year-to-date, nearly matching its record set in June.

The index covers semiconductors, memory, data centers, networking, power, and AI application companies.

At the same time, the S&P 500 Ex-AI Enablers Index has increased just +5%, underperforming by 53 percentage points.

Meanwhile, the semiconductor index is up +78% over the same period, with Micron, $MU, Marvell, $MRVL, Intel, $INTC, AMD, $AMD up +263%, +224%, +190 %, and +190%, respectively.

By comparison, the S&P 500 index is up +13% while the Nasdaq 100 is up +22% so far in 2026.

The AI trade is leaving the rest of the market far behind.

BREAKING: Total consumer credit rose +$8.3 billion in August, to a record $5.19 trillion.

This marks the 14th consecutive monthly increase, totalling +$154 billion.

Since the start of 2022, consumer credit has risen +$684 billion.

Non-revolving credit, covering auto and student loans, rose +$13.1 billion in August, to $3.84 trillion, an all-time high.

Meanwhile, revolving credit, which includes credit cards, fell -$4.8 billion, to $1.35 trillion, its 4th-highest level on record.

US consumers are still borrowing.
